messages.text: Norris wins wet Sao Paulo GP as Mercedes seal constructors' title

metadata.summary: McLaren's Lando Norris recovered from a poor start to claim a dominant victory in a wet Sao Paulo Grand Prix that saw Mercedes seal the 2026 Formula 1 Constructors' Championship.
metadata.content: Sao Paulo GP: Lando Norris wins wet race for McLaren as Mercedes seal 2026 F1 Constructors' Championship in Brazil | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Sao Paulo GP: Lando Norris wins wet race for McLaren as Mercedes seal 2026 F1 Constructors' Championship in Brazil Pole-sitter Lando Norris recovers from poor start to win Sao Paulo GP; Max Verstappen comes from 21st on grid to take second ahead of Red Bull team-mate Isack Hadjar; George Russell and Kimi Antonelli fourth and fifth, respectively, to seal Constructors' Championship for Mercedes Sunday 8 November 2026 21:40, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the 2026 Sao Paulo Grand Prix. McLaren's Lando Norris recovered from a poor start to claim a dominant victory in a wet Sao Paulo Grand Prix that saw Mercedes seal the 2026 Formula 1 Constructors' Championship. Max Verstappen produced a signature stunning drive in the wet to come from 21st on the grid to finish second, with his team-mate Isack Hadjar completing a double-podium for Red Bull. Newly crowned world champion Kimi Antonelli had looked on course for victory after taking the lead at the start but ultimately had to settle for fifth behind his team-mate George Russell, which was more than enough for Mercedes to establish an unassailable lead over Ferrari in the constructors' standings with three rounds to spare. Man Utd's 18th-place position is their lowest after 10 top-flight games since 1986/87, when they were 20th. messages.text: Villa boss Emery explains why he went down tunnel before full-time

metadata.summary: A prickly Unai Emery claimed he headed down the Old Trafford tunnel after Manchester United's late equaliser against his Aston Villa side because he thought the match was about to end.
metadata.content: Unai Emery: Aston Villa boss reveals why he went down Old Trafford tunnel before full-time in eight-goal thriller at Man Utd | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Unai Emery: Aston Villa boss reveals why he went down Old Trafford tunnel before full-time in eight-goal thriller at Man Utd Unai Emery headed down Old Trafford tunnel before full-time after Man Utd rescued a 4-4 draw against his Aston Villa team; Patrick Dorgu scored late equaliser in thrilling contest; Villa director of football operations Damian Vidagany questioned legitimacy of last goal Sunday 8 November 2026 20:35, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Aston Villa boss Unai Emery explains his decision to walk down the tunnel at Old Trafford after Manchester United nabbed their 96th minute equaliser. A prickly Unai Emery claimed he headed down the Old Trafford tunnel after Manchester United's late equaliser against his Aston Villa side because he thought the match was about to end. Villa threw away two separate two-goal leads to draw 4-4 with United in a Super Sunday thriller - but the 97th-minute equaliser from Michael Carrick's side, scored by Patrick Dorgu, brought about a strange reaction from Emery. The Villa manager was seen walking down the tunnel before the full-time whistle, with the match continuing for another two minutes before it ended. England head coach Steve Borthwick and captain Maro Itoje have rejected claims made in a newspaper article this week of a squad rift, saying it "does not represent the environment" they recognise. Speaking to media following Sunday's dominant 45-22 Nations Championship victory over Australia at Allianz Stadium Twickenham, Borthwick addressed the article for the first time since its publication on Friday. Within it, The Times reported that some England players lost faith in Borthwick during a summer campaign which included a 45-21 defeat to world champions South Africa and a nervy win over Argentina.
